annotation.authors_or_issuer: Republic of Korea (National Assembly; Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport)
annotation.venue: Korea Legislation Research Institute (KLRI) Korean Law Translation
annotation.summary_en: South Korea's Aviation Safety Act, as amended through May 2026, regulates aircraft registration, type and airworthiness certification, aviation personnel qualification, air operator certification, safety management systems and air traffic management. Unmanned aircraft appear only as ultra-light vehicles and in the accident definition; the Act has no AI-specific provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Aircraft must be registered, and type, production and airworthiness certification are required.
Ultra-light vehicles, including unmanned aerial vehicles, are defined by ministerial standards; unmanned aircraft operation is exempt from pilot qualification certification.
Aviation safety management systems and air operator certification are mandated, with validity inspections every five years.
The Minister must set a five-year master plan for aviation safety policy.
The Minister can revoke or suspend certifications and impose penalty surcharges of up to 100 million won.
